rationale: C18 plausibly supplied a material organizational template for the child. Both texts justify an agency reorganization, place a specialized operating organization within the foreign-affairs structure, designate a single director as the key official, prescribe direct reporting to the Secretary of State, preserve presidential involvement, and emphasize coordination with the Department of Defense and other agencies. C22 and C12 contain closely related foreign-affairs coordination machinery, but C18 offers the closest combination of concrete structure and language. The similarity is substantially more specific than the routine form used to transmit draft legislation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The proposed legislation provides that the Director of the new agency function under the direction of the President and the Secretary of State.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Two years ago I stated that the Secretary of State, under the President, must be the official responsible for the development and control of foreign policy... The policy authority then fixed in the Secretary of State is now extended to include supervising authority over operations.
shared_material.explanation: Both establish dual presidential and Secretary of State oversight over a specialized foreign-affairs operation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Director, as the principal adviser to the President in the disarmament field, will have direct access to him... In addition, the Director will report to the Secretary of State without going through intermediate authority
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Provision will be made for a Director... who will be the key official within the State Department... The Director... will report directly to the Secretary of State
shared_material.explanation: The direct-reporting director arrangement is a concrete and distinctive organizational parallel.

shared_material.child_excerpt: close working-level coordination and cooperation [must] be established between the new agency and the Departments of State and Defense, the Atomic Energy Commission, and other agencies
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Secretary of State will be responsible for coordinating all Mutual Security programs, which will of course include the establishment of arrangements with the Secretary of Defense for effectively coordinating Mutual Security programs involving the Department of Defense
shared_material.explanation: Both prescribe State-centered interagency coordination, specifically including Defense, for a specialized international-security program.
